correctness.rationale: Full standard-lattice facet inequalities x_i>=0,y_j>=0,x_i+y_j<=1 are proved; sign-flipped normal vectors form a rooted graphic incidence matrix, whose active columns are unimodular exactly for forests. An active cycle either forces a left or right coordinate equal to one or forces all four inequalities on a 2x2 rectangle to equality. Exactly these faces give p+q+binom(p,2)binom(q,2) maximal singular orbit closures; all proper support types are excluded. Local dual semigroups are explicitly S_q={(a,c):0<=c_j<=a}, giving the Segre (P1)^q Hilbert function (a+1)^q and multiplicity q!, or a square cone with uv-wz=0. Exact face-lattice enumeration for five small parameters and semigroup checks corroborate, without replacing, the symbolic proof. Main limitation: no singular-scheme or intersection-germ classification.

originality.rationale: Wagner (1996) already gives a general projective Hibi orbitwise smoothness criterion; it is not claimed as new. Lakshmibai--Mukherjee (2007) treat affine Hibi singular loci, Friedl (2015) identifies projective Hibi/order-polytope models and computes global divisor groups. The explicit two-parameter component families and generic transverse Segre-cone multiplicities were not located in the inspected full text and mathematical-index comparison. The complete Wagner article could not be read, leaving a material overlap risk, which is not presented as ruled out.
residual_risks: The entire Wagner 1996 original article was inaccessible; a fully worked case could supersede part or all of this claim.
Unindexed or differently termed projective Hibi/poset literature could include equivalent component counts and local Segre models.
Exact experiments only cover small part sizes; infinitude is proved by the active-graphic-cycle argument, not experiments.

value.rationale: The complete-bipartite stable-set/order-polytope family is canonical and doubly parameterized. The theorem precisely decomposes its singular support and demonstrates a genuine geometric transition: codimension-three conifolds coexist with Segre-cone strata of codimensions p+1 and q+1 and factorial generic multiplicity. Nonpure singular support in every case beyond K_{2,2} and the explicit face-model geometry give specific useful invariants not equivalent to merely applying a smoothness yes/no test. No downstream paper-sized application is asserted.
